## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 57, titled *Apavāraṇā* ("Not doing the invitation ceremony"), is an ecclesiastical rule in the Theravāda Vinaya governing the conduct of Buddhist nuns [SuttaCentral]. The rule stipulates that a nun who does not invite correction (*pavāraṇā*) regarding what has been seen, heard, or suspected from both the community of nuns and the community of monks upon completing the rains retreat incurs an offense requiring confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997]. A non-offense exemption applies if the nuns search for but cannot locate a Saṅgha of monks to invite [Sujato 2009].

Scholars observe that Pācittiya 57 is substantively and textually identical to the fourth *garudhamma* (heavy rule) [Sujato 2009; Hüsken 1997]. Ute Hüsken notes that this equivalence exposes an internal legal discrepancy within the Vinaya: while Garudhamma 5 assigns a fourteen-day period of discipline (*mānatta*) for the breach of any *garudhamma*, Pācittiya 57 punishes the same non-performance with simple confession [Hüsken 1997]. The ceremony and its associated procedures are also documented in the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20) with a distinct origin narrative [SuttaCentral; Sujato 2009].

According to SuttaCentral, full parallels to this rule are preserved in the Theravāda *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* (pc 57) and *Parivāra*, as well as in the nun's rules of the Dharmaguptaka (Bi Vb Pc 142), Mahīśāsaka (Bi Vb Pc 93), Sarvāstivāda (Bi Vb Pc 150 / 151), and Mūlasarvāstivāda traditions in Chinese (Pc 129) and Tibetan (Pc 166) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus records 239 Pali-internal text reuse matches across 74 texts, sharing long formulaic segments primarily with adjacent Vibhaṅga rules such as Pācittiya 58, Pācittiya 7, and Pācittiya 56 [DharmaNexus].
